content5.ptxt: The engine control computer controls the throttle valve opening (ISC flow rate) during idling. If deposits adhere to the throttle valve, the ISC flow rate decreases, which may lead to engine stalling or unstable idling, so the ISC flow rate required for idling is ensured by ISC learning and feedback.
When the ISC learned amount approaches the control limit, the engine control computer outputs a DTC.

entry.ptxt: When all of the following conditions are met, 1 trip is established.

item.ptxt: The engine is started with the coolant temperature at 45°C or less, then warmed up and the ISC learning conditions are met, or 1 hours or more have elapsed with IG ON, the engine is warmed up and the ISC learning conditions are met
There is a driving history of 30 km/h or more.
Intake air flow meter sub-assembly is normal
Atmospheric pressure is 85 kPa or more (altitude 1400 m or less)

entry.ptxt: ISC learned amount is approximately 3 times normal and intake air volume during idling is normal (within 1.5 times normal)
Detected 1 time(s) during 1 trip(s). (No detection after judgment.)

item.ptxt: Throttle body assembly with motor (throttle position sensor)
Using SST (TaSCAN), read the Freeze Frame Data. Freeze frame data records part of the engine operating condition when the malfunction occurred, and this information is useful when troubleshooting.

Since no pending code is stored for this DTC, confirming the repair by whether the DTC is output takes a long time. When confirming the repair, it can be done in a short time by comparing the ISC flow learned value stored in the freeze frame data with the ISC flow learned value after repair.

testgrp.testtitle: Check Freeze Frame Data (ISC Flow Rate Learned Value)

test1.ptxt: Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, check the ISC flow learned value at the time the DTC was detected using the freeze frame data. (see )

atten4.ptxt: Be sure to check this, as the ISC flow learned value stored in the freeze frame data is required when confirming the repair.

test1.ptxt: Check whether deposits have adhered to the inside of the throttle body assembly with motor.

test1.ptxt: Clean Throttle Body Assembly with Motor

test2.ptxt: Push the throttle valve open by hand and wipe the carbon off the valve and bore using a cloth or equivalent soaked in engine conditioner (for EFI vehicles).

item.ptxt: Be careful not to catch fingers, cloth, etc. in the valve.
Be careful not to let foreign matter enter.

Do not wash the throttle body assembly with motor in its entirety or spray engine conditioner (for EFI vehicles) directly onto it. Cleaning fluid may enter from the valve shaft and cause problems such as poor sliding or rust.
If a coating has been applied, be careful not to peel it off.

test1.ptxt: Remove the EFI MAIN fuse and ETCS fuse from the engine room R/B for 60 seconds or more to reset the ISC flow learned value.
Start the engine and warm it up until the engine coolant temperature stabilizes.
Leave the engine idling for 3 minutes or more and check that the engine speed is at the standard value.
Following the SST (TaSCAN) screen display, read [ECU Data Monitor] - [ISC Flow Learned Value].

specitem.ptxt: Lower than the ISC flow learned value stored in the freeze frame data.
